Before this, I worked in marketing for 8 years, which gave me strong problem-solving and project management skills. I've built a few personal projects including a web scraper for market research and a small Django application.

I'm relatively new to Python - about a year and a half of focused learning. My background is in marketing management, but I've always been interested in technology. I've completed several online courses and built some projects to practice what I've learned.

I have marketing experience but I've been dedicating myself to learning Python for the past 18 months. I've worked with basic web development, some data analysis, and I'm comfortable with the fundamentals, though I know I have a lot more to learn.

I decided to make this career change because I want work that's more technically challenging and creative. I chose Python because it seemed like a great entry point into development, and I love how logical and powerful it is.

Marketing taught me a lot about understanding user needs and solving problems, and I think those skills translate well to development. I'm excited about using Python to build solutions that can really make a difference.
